description:
FILED s536g (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) as #4603's residue.  #4603 made the call-site NAMING and the implicit-`$_` operand ask `Pl::Parser::gated_keyword_at`; the OPERAND GRAMMAR of a paren-less call still reads the builtin's facts (`fc` is a named unary in Config: `is_named_unary`, `collapse_extra_unary_params`, the [1,-2] spec).

    sub fc { "U(" . join(" ", @_) . ")" }
    my @r = (fc 1, 2);
    print scalar(@r), " $r[0]\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  1 U(1 2)        -- no feature: `fc` is the user's list operator
      PCL (s536g):  2 U(1)          -- the named-unary operand stops at the comma

With parens (`fc(1, 2)`) it is right.  The fix: the named-unary readers in PExpr (is_named_unary / collapse_extra_unary_params / the known_no_of_params spec at the operand site) ask the same `_gated_keyword_is_sub` the `$_` default asks, so a gated keyword that is a sub here parses by its prototype record (`no_params_of_sub` already reads the record first).  Probe `say` (a list operator either way; its `:fh` slot `say STDERR "x"` with a user sub is indirect-object syntax in perl), `isa` (infix with the feature), `evalbytes`.


=== DONE (s537a, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-10 .. 11-13; commit bada882f on the s537a branch, rebased over MAIN-READY-87; shas as of the rebase over main b620405f) ===
FIXED: where a feature-gated keyword (`fc` `say` `isa` `evalbytes`) is the USER's sub at the call site -- `Pl::Parser::gated_keyword_at` answering "not the keyword" -- every parse site that read the BUILTIN's facts now asks the same answer through ONE helper `PExpr::_gated_sub_here(NAME, HEAD-TOKEN)` (the head-token twin of s536g's `_gated_keyword_is_sub`): `is_named_unary` (the operand grammar -- `(fc 1, 2)` is fc(1, 2)), `no_params_of_sub` (a gated sub with no record of its own is a LIST operator; a `($)` user sub keeps its prototype), `collapse_extra_unary_params`, `child_context` (user-sub LIST context for the arguments), Parser2 `_word_takes_list`, `_fix_ppi_negative_number_bug`, and `is_token_operator` (the word `isa` is the infix operator only where the keyword is -- `sub isa {...} (isa 1, 2)` was a DROP, "Fell through", #4802).  `say FH LIST` with a user `say` is perl's indirect object FH->say(LIST) = IO::Handle::say = the builtin: the handle-slot site marks the head `_core_qualified`.
PROBES (scratch/s537a/p/m4a..m4j, perl / main 4a39a1c7 / tree): fixed m4a (fc / say / evalbytes list operator, 14 lines), m4b (say STDOUT with a user say), m4e (say STDERR), m4h (isa + evalbytes); controls identical on all three: m4c (STDOUT->say), m4d (fc($) prototype, CORE::fc, use feature 'fc' / 'say', no feature 'fc'), m4f (use v5.16 bundle), m4g (lc / uc, Foo::fc), m4i (infix isa under the feature), m4j (a class overriding UNIVERSAL::isa).
GUARD: Pl/t/runtime-name-hygiene-01.t rows 21-22 (inverse: main prints `2 fc(1) 2` and drops the isa statement).  Targeted gate tg4b 17 files / 804 PASS.  NAME-RESOLUTION change: the gate-SET scan over both populations is IDENTICAL (638 files) and the sweep is its gate (session log).
BARS (the combined tree over MAIN-READY-87, HEAD 7cd511ac): FULL gate 369 / 12,018 -> 12,046 PASS (+ tr-01.t row 9 = 12,047); FULL sweep GATE clean 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL 18,795 -> 18,796 (tr.t +1 = #1493, by edit), drops 5 = census; corpus-diff vs 23f0f917 3 / 111; wide emission A/B 2,053 files 29 DIFF explained / RCDIFF 0; gate-SET scan 638 files IDENTICAL over both populations; ir-host-leak 31 = 31; ir-conform 328 / 0; EVERYDAY 116 -> 116 of 122 (NEW 0); compile time unchanged (Calc.pm 5.52 -> 5.51 s).  Detail: docs/session-log.md, section s537a.
subject: #4603 residue: where a feature-gated keyword is a USER sub (`sub fc {...}` without the feature), its paren-less call still takes the builtin's named-unary operand -- `(fc 1, 2)` is (fc(1), 2) where perl calls fc(1, 2)
